messages.subject: Re: use renjin behind a proxy
messages.body_plain:
Dear Mathieu,

you are receiving this error because there is no artifact for the FactoMinR package in our repository. It is not available for Renjin at this time, see http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/FactoMineR. The problem is that it depends on the knitr package* which we cannot (yet) build for Renjin.

Regards,

Maarten-Jan

*) for reasons which I do not understand as it imports the "knit" function, but doesn't seem to do anything with it in the code. I will contact the author of the package to inquire about this.

messages.subject: Plotting in Renjin
messages.body_plain:
Last year I did some investigation of using renjin in one of my applications (which I still hope to do), but the lack of graphics was a major issue.  I did some experimentation (in part to learn about R and renjin, both of which are new to me).  I developed code to be able to use the plot and barplot commands which now have at least basic functionality.  As my own code uses JavaFX for the GUI, I first did this by developing code to drive the JavaFX chart library.   But real support of R graphics would require developing a true R Graphics Device, so I've also done some prototyping of this by developing a Graphics Device based on the JavaFX Canvas.

I'm not sure how fast I'll progress on this (or given my current work load whether it's feasible at all), but given that others are interested in graphics in renjin I thought I'd share the current state of the code.  Given that it's been done as a learning process and experiment, it's all fairly rough, but could be a useful starting point.

It can be found at:

https://github.com/brucejohnson/jfxplot

cheers,

Bruce

If you add a release tag, e.g. "v0.1" to the repo, I can add it to packages.renjin.org <http://packages.renjin.org>

Best,
Alex

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I've stumbled over org.renjin.graphics.device.AwtGraphicsDevice and was wondering if it would be possible to use it as an output graphics device in a native R session. The usecase would be to draw plots directly into an AWT/Swing panel.

So something like

dyn.load("~/some_renjin.dylib")
init_device <- function() { .Call("something") }
options(device=init_device)

Best regards,
Holger

Hi Holger,
Unfortunately, this class is left over from a very early, abandoned effort to essentially port the graphics and grDevices packages to Renjin, so I'm not sure if it's of much use either from within Renjin or from GNU R.

However, I think what you're looking does exist though I couldn't find the exact reference. You might start looking at the JGR project:
https://www.rforge.net/JGR/

Hope this helps,
Alex
